title: Nia and the Feather Songs
markdown:
A bright breezy morning held a puzzle. Sunlight dappled through the leaves. Sweet honeysuckle tickled Nia’s nose. Beside her wobbly treehouse lay a rainbow of soft bird feathers: sunshine-yellow, sky-blue, ladybug-red. Pebble the puppy yipped, tail a happy blur, and sat on one feather until Nia rescued it.

She wanted each feather in the right bird’s nest. The songs sounded jumbled, overlapping, as if the trees were arguing politely. “This yellow feather,” she whispered, holding it up. “It has a fast, wiggly song!” Pebble nudged a blue one. “Not your nose, Pebble!” She giggled and moved the blue out of lick range.

Ms. Lark, a songbird with shiny amber feathers, landed nearby. “A puzzle?” Her voice a gentle melody.

“I can’t tell which feather belongs to which bird.”

Lark hopped closer. “The songs are like messages.” She trilled a high, clear note. “High. A tall, thin line.” Then a deeper warble. “Low. A soft, round pillow.”

Nia closed her eyes and listened. High and fast, like quick waves. Low and slow, like big ones. Eyes wide. “The high songs belong with the bright, fast-looking feathers. Like this yellow one.” Pebble gave a soft woof of agreement, or of wanting the feather; it was hard to say.

She matched bright chirps to the quick yellow and red. She matched cozy hums to the softer, duskier blues. One nest got two yellows and she had to listen again, head tilted, until the second chirp told her the truth. Soon every feather sat in the right nest. The birds sang their own special songs, a happy tune for everyone, and Pebble stopped barking long enough to hear it.

Lark beamed and named it once: pitch. Some sounds high, a playful leap. Some low, a gentle rest. She did not send Nia hunting every rustle for secrets.

Nia looked at the trees, the birds, Pebble’s wagging tail. The puzzle was solved. A happy hum of discovery. She tucked one spare sky-blue feather into the treehouse crack as a reminder of the low pillow-song, and left the rest to their proper owners.
